subject: mathematics
question_text: Apply the test of rank to examine whether the system x + y + z = 6, x − y + z = 2, 2x − y + 3z = 9 is consistent, and if consistent find the complete solution.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.103 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 154. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed SAQ on its length and shape. The bank heading gives no section, so this classification is OURS. It is a genuinely different TECHNIQUE from Unit 3's LAQ system-solving — the rank test decides consistency BEFORE any solution is attempted. Printed appearances: AP 19. The rank test answers a question the other methods cannot: whether a solution EXISTS at all. Comparing rank(A) with rank[A D] is what decides it. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular 1x7 for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

steps.label: Write the augmented matrix
steps.margin_note: First mark. Same opening as Gauss-Jordan — the coefficient matrix with the constants attached.
steps.memory_tip: Same opening as Gauss-Jordan: the coefficient matrix with the constants attached.
lines: The system is AX = D, where

recall.must_convey: That the augmented matrix [A | D] is written.
accept: write the augmented matrix with the constants attached
form A given D
set up the augmented matrix
augmented matrix rasta
attach the constants to the coefficient matrix

steps.why: The rank test needs BOTH matrices — A and [A D] — so the augmented form is what carries them together.
common_mistakes: Putting the constants in as a row.

steps.label: Reduce to echelon form
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Row-reduce until the shape is triangular. The operations are the same as Gauss-Jordan, but the purpose is different — this is about counting, not solving.
steps.memory_tip: Same operations as Gauss-Jordan, but the PURPOSE is different — this is about counting ranks.

recall.must_convey: That row operations reduce the augmented matrix to echelon form with 1s down the diagonal.
accept: row reduce to echelon form with ones on the diagonal
apply the row operations until it is triangular
reduce the augmented matrix
row operations tho echelon form ki teeskuravali
get it into echelon form

steps.why: Rank is read off the echelon form, so reducing is not optional — the ranks of the original matrices are invisible until it is done.
common_mistakes: Trying to read the rank off the original matrix.
Stopping before the form is triangular.

steps.label: Compare the two ranks
steps.margin_note: Third mark, and the actual test. The coefficient part has a non-zero 3×3 determinant, so rank(A) = 3; the augmented matrix has no extra non-zero row, so rank[A D] = 3 too.
steps.memory_tip: The test itself: equal ranks means consistent, and rank = number of unknowns means one solution.
lines: ∴ Rank(A) = Rank[A D] = 3 = number of unknowns,
so the system is CONSISTENT with a unique solution.

recall.must_convey: That rank(A) = rank[A D] = 3 = the number of unknowns, so the system is consistent with a unique solution.
accept: both ranks are three which equals the number of unknowns so it is consistent with a unique solution
rank A equals rank of the augmented matrix so it is consistent
three equals three equals the number of unknowns
rendu ranks three, unknowns moodu, so consistent unique solution
compare the ranks to decide consistency

steps.why: Equal ranks mean consistent; equal to the number of unknowns means the solution is unique. If the ranks differed the system would have NO solution, and no amount of solving would find one.
common_mistakes: Concluding consistency without comparing the two ranks.
Forgetting to compare against the number of unknowns.

steps.label: Read off the solution
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The echelon form is already three equations — read z and y directly, then back-substitute for x.
steps.memory_tip: The echelon form is already three equations — read z and y, then back-substitute for x.

recall.must_convey: That the echelon rows give y = 2, z = 3 and back-substitution gives x = 1.
accept: the rows give y equals two and z equals three then back substitute to get x equals one
read off y and z then find x
the solution is one two three
y two, z three, x one vasthundi
back substitute for x

steps.why: This form stops at echelon rather than going all the way to the identity, so one back-substitution is still needed — unlike Gauss-Jordan, which clears upwards too.
common_mistakes: Reading x straight off without substituting.
Reporting the ranks as the answer.

insider_note: Row-reduce the AUGMENTED matrix once and read both ranks off it — computing them separately doubles the work. Equal ranks matching the number of unknowns is what consistent-and-unique means.
